children: Primark owner Associated British Foods reported a rise in revenue for the full fiscal year, but expects its sugar business to continue weighing on results.

The U.K. conglomerate booked 19.58 billion pounds ($26.25 billion)  in revenue compared with 19.46 billion pounds a year earlier. However, many other headline figures were in the red, with pretax profit falling 10% to 1.28 billion pounds for the year.
For its retail business, which houses the Primark brand, AB Foods said Tuesday that sales rose 2% to 9.8 billion pounds for the year.

The sugar-to-shirts conglomerate is in the process of splitting fast-fashion arm Primark from its food units, with completion expected by December 2027. Its foods business--encompassing ingredients, sugar, agriculture and grocery--has traditionally been less favored by investors than the retail business.

AB Foods' sugar business posted an adjusted operating loss of 47 million pounds in the fiscal year, linked to lower average selling prices in Europe. The loss is expected to deepen to a range of 70 million to 170 million pounds for the following year.

It also tempered its expectations for the grocery segment from its previous update in September. It now expects grocery earnings before interest and taxes broadly flat on year, when it previously saw the metric slightly ahead of the 2026 fiscal year's level.

The slight grocery outlook cut reflects how cocoa prices won't fall as steeply as expected, and the margin pressures from a challenging consumer environment, according to a note from Barclays analyst Matthew Clements.
Though the segment's downgrade is disappointing, it won't taint sentiment too much, Clements wrote.
